item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q018_tal_effector_repeat_lengths","answer":"SCOPe groups d2kq5a_, d3v6pa_, and d4cj9a_ in TAL effector family a.298.1.1 because each contains the homologous TAL-effector DNA-binding repeat architecture: tandem, approximately 34-residue, mostly α-helical units with the characteristic repeat-variable diresidue loop. Their total lengths differ because d2kq5a_ is a short repeat-region construct, whereas d3v6pa_ and d4cj9a_ contain substantially larger repeat arrays; biological repeat copy number and deposited construct boundaries both vary. Thus length chiefly records how many homologous modules were included, not a different structural family. Hierarchically, a.298.1.1 is the family-level assignment within superfamily a.298.1, fold a.298, and all-α class a; fold or class agreement alone would not establish homology, while the common family supports a much stronger evolutionary relationship for the repeat domains. The assignment does not imply identical full-length proteins, repeat counts, or DNA targets: differences in repeat-variable diresidues can change base specificity, so target or function annotations should not be transferred solely from family membership. For structural modeling, individual repeats may provide local templates, but whole-array templates should be chosen to match repeat number, RVD pattern, construct boundaries, and DNA-bound state; the longest entry is not automatically the best representative.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
